_when_written: Phase 6.1, WHILE the arm runs were still executing and BEFORE any arm output existed on disk. Verifiable from the coordinator ledger: the coordinator turn that wrote this file overlaps the six measure.* run windows and precedes every one of their end timestamps.
_why_this_is_allowed: chain.contract.json blinding_order.exception: 'An expectation whose correct answer is computed from a fixture rather than judged - a cut score, a count, a rate - may be written from the fixture at any time, because no arm's output can move it.' Every expectation below is computed from logged_traffic.csv by pipeline/builds/eval-set-curation-v2/measure/fixture_facts.json. None of them can be moved by what any arm said.
_the_correction_that_makes_this_matter: The package's ground_truth.json says 6 near-duplicate clusters over 120 rows. Under THIS SKILL'S OWN step 1 that is wrong, and the whole-artefact reviewer found it: normalising IDs and digits as step 1 clause 1 instructs leaves 64 distinct strings over the whole file, of which 4 cover the 1880 placeholder rows and 60 cover the 120 real-text rows. So the number a correct run reports is about 10 families, not 6. Graded against the package figure, a correct answer would have scored as a miss. E1 and E3 below are written against the corrected structure.

expectations.question: Q3
expectations.expectation: The answer treats the 1880 placeholder rows as a near-duplicate FAMILY, not as 1880 unique rows. Any of these counts as meeting it: reporting them as one family per slice; reporting a distinct-string count near 64 after normalisation; or saying explicitly that normalising the case number and hash collapses them.
expectations.computed_from: distinct strings after normalising 8-hex tokens and digits = 64; 4 of those cover 1880 rows
expectations.meets_it_partially: finds the 60 exact-duplicate pairs among the 120 real-text rows and stops there - this is what 3 of 4 probe runs did
expectations.third_defensible_answer_admitted_now_not: A run may argue that the placeholder rows are each their OWN cluster because there is no text to compare - probe.A.without.r1 did exactly that in the curate.py it wrote, with the comment 'Opaque placeholder rows have no usable text -> each is its own cluster'. That is a reasoned position, not the failure F1 describes, and it MEETS this expectation provided the reasoning is stated. What does NOT meet it is passing over the 1880 rows in silence. This clause is added at phase 6.1, from a PROBE transcript, BEFORE any arm output was read and before the blinding - recorded here so that admitting it later could not be mistaken for loosening the expectation to fit an answer.

expectations.question: Q3
expectations.expectation: TWO de-duplication numbers are reported separately - a distinct-string count and a distinct-cluster/family count - rather than one number standing for both.

expectations.question: Q4
expectations.expectation: The reporting floor is derived from a stated tolerance (a half-width the team can act on, or a difference the gate must detect), not asserted as a round number. A floor with a citation but no tolerance does NOT meet this.
expectations.computed_from: not a number - this is the one judgement-shaped expectation in this file, and it is here rather than in the post-blinding set because it is the literal text of the skill's step 2 and could be written from the artefact alone

expectations.question: Q4
expectations.expectation: The per-slice interval is computed, and the adversarial slice at n=22 is stated to be unusable for a per-slice claim. The measured Wilson 95% half-widths are 1.1 points (simple_lookup, n=1647), 5.6 (multi_hop, n=264), 11.6 (ambiguous, n=67) and 18.2 (adversarial, n=22). An answer whose adversarial half-width is not within 2 points of 18.2 has computed it wrongly.
expectations.note: the probe showed 4 of 4 baseline runs already do this, so this is a REGRESSION GUARD and not a discriminator

expectations.note: the probe showed 4 of 4 baseline runs already do this. The skill MAY NOT LOSE IT.
